topics.title: When are vibe checks enough?
topics.summary: Guests treat vibe checks as the first eval, and agree they stop working once more people use the product or more people work on it.

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: I actually think vibe checks are a form of eval

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: Your vibe checks are very important, but they don't scale because they involve you, the human.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: I've never seen somebody make it through multiple iterations of their product without any evals.

topics.title: How do you decide what to evaluate?
topics.summary: Start by reading real outputs, write notes on what went wrong, and group the notes into failure modes. Evals come after that.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: after going through about 100 of those, they will try to merge similar notes together into clusters. And this determines your failure modes.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: you should be grounding it in things that are going wrong or the things that will probably go wrong.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Torres
quotes.quote: we're going to literally have humans review them and tag them where there are errors

quotes.speaker: Teresa Torres
quotes.quote: for errors that are kind of persistent, I'm going to write an eval.

topics.title: How do you trust an LLM judge?
topics.summary: Label examples by hand, measure the judge against your labels, and fix the judge where it disagrees.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: 80% of people who are using LLM as a judge are just writing a prompt and just praying that is doing the right thing.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: how do I make this judge a proxy of me? And how do I trust it? Almost like an employee.

quotes.speaker: Aman Khan
quotes.quote: I don't see too many people actually, when they talk about evals saying that you need to check the work of the LLM as a judge

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: people will keep changing the rubric as they encounter new failure modes when looking at the data.

topics.title: Pass/fail or a 1-to-5 score?
topics.summary: Guests who build judges recommend binary criteria, because models apply them more reliably than fine-grained scales.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: we say limit yourself to binary, because that is what the LLM can do very well.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: In our course, we define that as a rubric of binary criteria.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: I've never seen just one eval doing the job. I see three to five, sometimes even up to 10 evals that are really important for a product.

topics.title: What goes in a golden dataset?
topics.summary: Inputs, optionally expected answers, and enough hard cases that the current system fails some of them.

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: An eval consists of three things.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: Think about it as like a pre-baked set of trivia questions that you ask the model.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: you want to score like, you know, 25 to 50% on these evals.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: if you're getting 100% accuracy in your evals, it's likely your evals are worthless because they are providing you with no signal.

topics.title: Offline or online evals?
topics.summary: Offline evals decide whether to ship. Online evals check whether users actually got what the offline set predicted.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: let's ship it into prod and see if they actually like it with an online eval.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: performance on that offline eval set will reflect the satisfaction of the user in the online eval. This obviously doesn't always happen

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: Every week or so, I'll sample some of my traces, run my LLM-powered evaluators on them, and then kind of just look at the score, see if anything's off or whatnot.

topics.title: How do evals change cost and latency decisions?
topics.summary: An eval set is what lets you try a cheaper model and know whether quality held. Latency is judged at p95, not on averages.

quotes.speaker: Ankit Shukla
quotes.quote: They can let you understand whether a cheaper model can also go ahead and perform at a similar kind of level or not.

quotes.speaker: Ankit Shukla
quotes.quote: because in prototypes we are using the best kind of models because we want to show the prototypes in the best light

quotes.speaker: Ankit Shukla
quotes.quote: we will have the latency so p50 p95 p99 means that whenever we do averaging averaging is not going to give you the right kind of results

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: evals are not free.

topics.title: How do you evaluate an agent?
topics.summary: Score whole tasks rather than single answers, and look at the steps, because that is where an agent's failures hide.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: this is a totally new paradigm of writing evals because you're no longer thinking about QA, you're thinking about tasks.

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: I set it up to evaluate every step. Maybe you only want to evaluate the last step

quotes.speaker: Aman Khan
quotes.quote: it's a line of code that you implement on top of your functions.

topics.title: How do you test safety and guardrails?
topics.summary: Guests treat guardrails as part of the eval plan: say what the product must not do, test it, red-team it continuously, and re-measure after every change.

quotes.speaker: Ankit Shukla
quotes.quote: And then guardrails. This is a major part. where evals actually shine which is you are going to define what should the model do what should the product do what should it not do

quotes.speaker: Jake Brill
quotes.quote: We do red teaming not just for new launches, but for our products all across the board.

quotes.speaker: Jake Brill
quotes.quote: there's a lot of work that we do to mitigate prompt injection, to make sure that the agents are acting in a reliable fashion.

quotes.speaker: Greg Greiner
quotes.quote: you need to have the appropriate guardrails in place and you need to be thinking about every update you make. And measuring them against both those guardrails as well as continuing to do some level of human QA.

topics.title: Who should own the evals?
topics.summary: Guests put the PM at the centre, because evals are where product judgment turns into something a team can run.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: evals give you a way as a PM to inject your taste and your judgment directly into the critical path of the AI product being developed.

quotes.speaker: Jake Brill
quotes.quote: PMs oftentimes are the ones with the clearest vision of how the product should work in their head

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: I think the modern PRD is an eval.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: You don't want to give up that leverage because when you build that foundation of evals, you develop, you have immense leverage
